cleared.name: Bruce K. MacLaury (President, Minneapolis Fed, 1971-1977)
cleared.reason: New York Fed, US Treasury, Minneapolis Fed, then president of the Brookings Institution, a non-profit research organisation, until 1995.

cleared.name: Robert C. Holland (Governor, Board of Governors, 1973-1976)
cleared.reason: After the Board he was president of the Committee for Economic Development, a non-profit, 1976-90, then a senior fellow at the Wharton School.

cleared.name: Watrous H. Irons (President, Dallas Fed, 1954-1968)
cleared.reason: University of Texas faculty and the Office of Price Administration before the Dallas Fed; he died in office in 1968. No private employer named.

cleared.name: Edward M. Gramlich (Governor, Board of Governors, 1997-2005)
cleared.reason: Board of Governors staff, Office of Economic Opportunity, Brookings, University of Michigan, Congressional Budget Office, then the Urban Institute in 2006. No private financial employer named.

logged.name: Mark H. Willes (President, Minneapolis Fed, 1977-1980)
logged.detail: private but not financial employer — the page states that in 1980 he left the Minneapolis Fed to become chief financial officer at General Mills, a food manufacturer.

logged.name: Charles J. Scanlon (President, Chicago Fed, 1962-1970)
logged.detail: private but not financial employer — the page states he took early retirement from the Chicago Fed and accepted a position as vice president at General Motors Corporation in New York.

logged.name: John E. Sheehan (Governor, Board of Governors, 1972-1975)
logged.detail: private but not financial employers — McKinsey and Company (consulting) 1960-63, Martin Marietta Corporation, Corhart Refractories Company (a Corning Glass Works subsidiary), Orion Broadcasting Company, and after the Board, Williamsport Wirerope Works Inc., a steel-cable plant he bought in 1989 and sold in 2004.

logged.name: Hugh D. Galusha Jr. (President, Minneapolis Fed, 1965-1971)
logged.detail: private but not financial employer — the page states he was head of his own CPA and tax law firm for many years and was a director on the Minneapolis Fed's board of directors when he was appointed president. He died in office in 1971.

logged.name: J. Roger Guffey (President, Kansas City Fed, 1976-1991)
logged.detail: private but not financial employer — the page states he practised law as a partner in the Kansas City law firm Fallon, Guffey and Jenkins for ten years before joining the Kansas City Fed as general counsel in 1968. After retiring in 1991 the page names no employer.

logged.name: Lyle E. Gramley — first post-Fed role
logged.detail: private but not a financial firm — chief economist at the Mortgage Bankers Association of America, an industry trade association, and later senior adviser at Potomac Research Group. His Schwab and Soleil Securities moves are recorded as a map record.

logged.name: Robert P. Forrestal — non-financial board seats
logged.detail: private but not financial employers — the Atlanta law firm Smith, Gambrell & Russell, and board seats at Equifax Inc. (credit reporting) and Genuine Parts Co. (auto-parts distribution). His ING roles are recorded as a map record.

logged.name: Mark W. Olson — Ernst & Young and Corporate Risk Advisors
logged.detail: private but not financial firms — national director of Ernst & Young LLP's regulatory consulting practice for the financial services industry 1988-1999, and cochairman of Corporate Risk Advisors LLC, a consulting and advisory firm, from September 2009. His banking roles are recorded as a map record.

logged.name: Roger W. Ferguson Jr. — pre-Fed employers
logged.detail: private but not financial firms — attorney at Davis Polk & Wardwell 1981-84 and partner at McKinsey & Company, Inc. 1984-87. His Swiss Re and TIAA-CREF moves are recorded as a map record.

logged.name: Allan Sproul — Kaiser Aluminum
logged.detail: private but not a financial firm — director of Kaiser Aluminum and Chemical Corporation. His Wells Fargo directorship is recorded as a map record.

logged.name: W. Braddock Hickman — American Airlines
logged.detail: private but not a financial firm — director of economic research and then assistant vice president at American Airlines. His New York Life role is recorded as a map record.
